items.headline: Gold/silver miners crushed far harder than metals after hot CPI repricing (GDX -5.4%, SILJ -5.7 to -6.4%)
items.summary: On Tue 11/10 GDX fell roughly 5.4% and SILJ 5.7-6.4% while spot gold/silver were down only ~2.7-3.4%, as the hot CPI print drove a sharp repricing of Fed hike odds. The move partially unwound the prior week's rally, with miner operating leverage amplifying the metals' pullback.
items.actionable: Levered silver/miner positions took the day's biggest drawdown on operating-leverage amplification of a modest metals pullback; this is forced/technical de-risking around a hawkish Fed repricing, not a change in the physical-tightness thesis, so it argues against panic-selling into the dip.

items.headline: October CPI runs hot (headline +0.4% vs +0.3% consensus, core +0.3% vs +0.2%), Fed Dec hike odds hit 100%
items.summary: BLS data released 21:30 SGT showed headline CPI +0.4% m/m (consensus +0.3%) and core CPI +0.3% m/m (consensus +0.2%), driven by broad-based food, goods and services pressure; y/y readings were 3.7% headline and 2.6% core. CME FedWatch moved to pricing a 100% probability of a December rate increase (89% quarter-point, 11% half-point), up from 84% the day before, after Fed Governor Waller said he'd back a hike and possibly a larger move, and Dallas Fed's Logan said two more hikes are needed.
items.actionable: The Fed pivoting toward hiking (not cutting) in December is the key macro risk for this book: higher real yields are the direct headwind hitting gold/silver miners and crypto hardest, while a stronger case for a higher-for-longer USD complicates HK/SG asset translation.

items.headline: Silver stays in backwardation with COMEX vaults draining and Shanghai premium elevated, even as price pulls back
items.summary: Registered COMEX silver inventory has fallen to 103.65 Moz, down roughly 48% from the September 2025 record high of 201 Moz, with continued net withdrawals pointing to physical tightness. Global silver ETF holdings have actually risen to their highest since March, with net inflows since Oct 30, even as the futures price corrected on Tuesday.
items.actionable: Persistent COMEX backwardation and vault drawdown alongside Tuesday's price/miner selloff suggests the pullback is a leverage/positioning flush rather than a fundamentals break, supporting staying long the silver/miner thesis through the volatility rather than reducing it.

items.headline: Nvidia board opens independent probe into Jensen Huang over alleged Chinese-spy affair; Huang summoned to Congress for Nov 18 briefing
items.summary: Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation, assisted by outside counsel, after reports that CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with a Chinese national US intelligence believes was feeding information to Beijing; Huang admitted the affair in a memo to staff. Nvidia shares fell 4.3% on the news, and three House Republican committee chairs demanded a closed-door briefing with Huang on Nov 18, one day after Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings.
items.actionable: A US-China tech-espionage scandal tied to Nvidia's CEO right before its Nov 17 earnings and SMIC's Nov 12 earnings raises the odds of tighter export-control rhetoric/scrutiny on China chip access, a sentiment headwind for SMIC and the broader China-tech complex even though SMIC itself is not directly implicated.

items.headline: Singapore banks' Q3 split (OCBC beats, DBS/UOB miss) but STI still rallies 1.53% as S-REITs trade mixed
items.summary: In Q3 2026 results reported across Nov 4-7, OCBC was the only one of the three Singapore banks to beat estimates, posting a record S$1.90B net profit (+16% YoY), while DBS and UOB both missed amid rising bond yields and higher deposit costs; all three shares fell during results week. Despite that and the global hot-CPI pullback, the Straits Times Index climbed 1.53% to 5,258.59 on Nov 10, and the FTSE ST REIT Index rose 0.34% with 14 of 39 S-REITs up.
items.actionable: The STI's resilience and OCBC's beat versus DBS/UOB's misses argue for staying selective within the SGX bank/REIT sleeve -- OCBC's margin discipline looks relatively better-positioned than DBS/UOB into a higher-for-longer Fed, while industrial/logistics REITs are the weak spot to watch versus firmer retail/commercial names.

items.headline: SMIC heads into Nov 12 earnings with analysts expecting ~31% revenue growth and margins within guidance
items.summary: Ahead of its Nov 12 report, analysts polled by Visible Alpha expect SMIC Q3 revenue of $3.12B (+31% YoY, +3.65% QoQ) and net profit of $396.8M, implying EPS growth of about 135% YoY; projected gross margin of 26.9% sits within the company's 26-28% guidance range. Investors will focus on order trends, pricing and AI-chip-driven demand commentary.
items.actionable: SMIC's Nov 12 print lands amid heightened US-China chip-security scrutiny from the Nvidia/Huang affair; a beat-and-raise would be a strong positive catalyst for the HK tech book, while any guidance disappointment would compound the already cautious China-chip sentiment.

items.headline: China's October trade surplus narrows to $105.3B but YTD surplus tops $1 trillion; semiconductor exports +137% YoY
items.summary: China's October trade surplus came in at $105.28B, narrower than September's $133.5B as imports (+41.6% YoY) outpaced the still-strong 35.2% YoY export surge; exports hit $412.33B for the month. Semiconductor exports value jumped 137.1% YoY and auto exports rose 37.6% YoY, while the Jan-Oct cumulative surplus reached a record $1.04 trillion.
items.actionable: Surging Chinese semiconductor export values support the structural growth narrative behind SMIC ahead of its Nov 12 earnings, while the narrowing headline surplus and import rebound signal some domestic demand recovery that is modestly supportive for HK-listed China consumer/tech names.

items.headline: Tencent heads into Nov 18 earnings with new Hy4 AI model central to the investment case
items.summary: Tencent is entering its final stretch before Q3 results on Nov 18, with artificial intelligence now central to the investor debate; the company announced its Hy4 model on Nov 4, integrating it into WorkBuddy, CodeBuddy and Tencent Cloud to broaden distribution. The report will test whether AI investment is translating into adoption, revenue and margin gains.
items.actionable: Tencent's Nov 18 print (one day after Nvidia's own earnings/Huang scrutiny) is a key near-term catalyst for the HK tech sleeve; a strong AI-monetization update would help offset the sentiment drag from the Nvidia espionage headlines on the broader China/AI trade.

items.headline: Rare-earth stocks diverge: MP Materials price targets cut after Q3 even as GM magnet deal advances; Lynas gets BMO 'Outperform' initiation
items.summary: MP Materials reported Q3 2026 results Nov 5 with heavy rare-earth separation and GM magnet shipments advancing, but Barclays cut its price target to $54 from $65 even as MP won attention for completing GM magnet qualification. Separately, BMO Capital initiated coverage of Lynas Rare Earths at 'Outperform' with an A$17 target on record prices, and Lynas shares rose 6.8% on Nov 9 to A$13.15.
items.actionable: The divergence -- MP facing target cuts despite genuine magnet-qualification progress, Lynas getting a fresh bullish initiation -- suggests the rare-earth watchlist should differentiate by balance-sheet/offtake progress rather than trade on the sector as one basket, especially with China's truce extension reducing near-term urgency for Western substitutes.

items.headline: China's MOFCOM extends rare-earth/battery/graphite export-control truce to January 10, 2027
items.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce issued Announcement No. 58 on Nov 9, one day before the original suspension's expiry, extending the pause on rare-earth, lithium-battery and graphite-anode export controls through Jan 10, 2027. Crucially, the April licensing requirements on seven medium/heavy rare earths including dysprosium and terbium were NOT lifted and remain in force.
items.actionable: The truce extension removes an immediate supply-shock catalyst that would have forced Western buyers toward MP Materials/Lynas on short notice, reducing urgency for the rare-earth watchlist's near-term re-rating thesis, even though the still-binding heavy-rare-earth licensing regime keeps the longer-term de-risking case intact.

items.headline: Qatar PM presents Trump an $8B Hormuz-reopening proposal; Trump calls Iran war 'effectively over', Rubio skeptical
items.summary: Qatar's prime minister met Trump at the White House Nov 9 and presented a two-phase Iranian proposal: Iran halts tanker/ship attacks and reopens the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the US lifting its naval/economic blockade and releasing $8B of Iranian funds held in Qatar. Trump called the war 'effectively over' militarily, but Secretary of State Rubio called the proposal unrealistic and the deal remains unconfirmed by either government.
items.actionable: A credible (if unconfirmed) path to de-escalating the Hormuz conflict is bearish for the safe-haven/geopolitical-risk premium embedded in gold and silver and for oil, but a confirmed deal would be a relief rally for risk assets broadly including HK tech and SGX names exposed to global trade flows.

items.headline: Crude slips toward $86-92/bbl as Hormuz de-escalation hopes offset ongoing tanker-attack risk
items.summary: WTI crude fell to roughly $86.44/bbl (-0.47%) and Brent to $92.06/bbl (-0.55%) on Nov 10, stabilizing after Monday's sharper drop on hopes that the Qatar-brokered proposal could end the Strait of Hormuz conflict, even as ship-tracker Kpler reports at least 18 vessels attacked in the strait over the past two weeks.
items.actionable: Falling oil on de-escalation hopes reduces the geopolitical inflation/energy-shock tail risk that has been a secondary tailwind for the silver/miners trade and for the cash pile's real-rate calculus; a reversal back toward conflict would quickly re-ignite that premium.

items.headline: Bitcoin falls below $75k to a near three-month low as hot CPI drives Fed hike bets and ETF outflows continue
items.summary: Bitcoin fell to roughly $73,874 (Ethereum and Solana both underperforming further) on Nov 10 after the hotter-than-expected CPI print pushed Fed rate-hike odds higher; BTC posted its lowest close in roughly three months. Spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen roughly $1.5B of net outflows since Nov 2, removing a key source of buying pressure.
items.actionable: Crypto is now trading as a high-beta rate-sensitive risk asset rather than a safe haven, falling in lockstep with the same hawkish-Fed repricing hitting silver miners; it reinforces that this CPI shock is a broad risk-off event across the portfolio's high-beta sleeves, not metals-specific.
